scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 5 · Measurement of Length and Motion
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, safety certification, traffic study or permission for hazardous physical measurement activities.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 5 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and observable mastery criterion while preserving measurement and motion safety boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner starts an object at a non-zero ruler mark and reports the final scale reading as the object's length.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a teacher-provided ruler diagram or stable tabletop object, record initial and final readings with units, and calculate final minus initial when the object does not begin at zero.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly solves unfamiliar zero-start and non-zero-start examples, includes the unit and explains why final-minus-initial gives the length.

scenarios.need: Learner reads a scale from an angle, omits units or believes extra decimal places automatically make a result more accurate.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare teacher-provided scale-reading diagrams, identify eye-level alignment and instrument resolution, and report only precision supported by the marked divisions.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Chooses the defensible reading from unfamiliar diagrams, states a suitable unit and rejects unsupported extra decimal places.

scenarios.need: Learner measures only the straight distance between the endpoints of a curved line and assumes it equals the curved path length.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a flat paper/card scenario with non-stretch string following the curve, mark the endpoints, straighten the string gently and measure the marked section without wrapping cord around a person.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains why endpoint distance may underestimate the curved path and selects an appropriate flexible method for unfamiliar safe curves.

scenarios.need: Learner stretches thread during measurement or treats small differences across repeats as proof that one reading is wrong.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare repeated hypothetical readings made with the same non-stretch method and report a sensible result or range consistent with the instrument instead of inventing precision.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Interprets small repeat variation appropriately and states how stretching, placement and scale resolution can affect the result.

scenarios.need: Learner says an object is simply moving or not moving without identifying a reference point.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Analyse toy-car, seat and fixed-marker cards and state the reference point before deciding whether position changes relative to it.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly gives different motion/rest descriptions for unfamiliar scenarios when the reference point changes.

scenarios.need: Learner confuses rectilinear, circular and periodic motion or assumes one motion category determines speed or cause.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort teacher-provided tabletop/video scenarios by observed path or repetition and explain when more than one description can apply without inferring speed or cause from the category alone.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Distinguishes straight-path, circular-path and repeating-time descriptions and justifies each classification using observable evidence.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes collecting motion data by standing near traffic, chasing a vehicle, leaning from a moving vehicle, using an escalator as an experiment or approaching machinery.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the hazardous plan and replace it with a stable tabletop toy, fixed tape marks or teacher-provided video; do not collect precise location, live vehicle tracking or device motion data.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Consistently identifies unsafe real-world motion-data plans and substitutes a controlled classroom model that answers the same reference-point question.

scenarios.need: Learner needs concise offline measurement and motion practice without uploading photos, location, sensor data or personal information.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, ruler diagrams and hypothetical motion cards locally; complete unit, subtraction and reference-point tasks without photo upload, GPS, accelerometer, microphone, camera or network-dependent tutoring.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline evidence task using only supplied synthetic material and explains the measurement/motion reasoning without personal or sensor-data disclosure.
